subject.title: [Feature]: Feishu Group Chat SubAgents for User-Specific Skills and Memory

question: Should OpenClaw support automatic per-sender Feishu group subagents, and if so should that be a narrow opt-in Feishu plugin feature, a generic channel/plugin API, or deferred in favor of existing session-scope and binding primitives?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the requested design chooses a new orchestration, config, skill, memory, and security boundary that automation should not invent without maintainer intent.

options.title: Narrow Feishu Opt-In
options.body: Design an explicit Feishu plugin feature for per-sender or per-topic group isolation, with lifecycle caps and security docs, while avoiding a new default agent hierarchy.

options.title: Use Existing Primitives
options.body: Keep this as documented groupSessionScope, bindings, broadcast groups, and DM-only dynamic agents, and close or redirect broader per-user behavior to smaller issue-specific improvements.

options.title: Generic API First
options.body: Defer Feishu implementation until generic channel threading, user skill preferences, and group context policies are settled as reusable plugin APIs.

recommendation.title: Narrow Feishu Opt-In
recommendation.body: Design an explicit Feishu plugin feature for per-sender or per-topic group isolation, with lifecycle caps and security docs, while avoiding a new default agent hierarchy.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision spans Feishu docs, plugin boundaries, config compatibility, and product guardrails where steipete has the strongest recent cross-surface history.
